title: Nand Kishor v. State of U.P. and another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; liberty to file para 6.8 objection; coercive action stayed.
headnote: In a writ seeking to quash recovery pursuant to a notice dated 19.08.2021 for Rs.53,632, the Allahabad High Court, without expressing any opinion on merits, disposed of the petition by granting the consumer liberty to submit an objection under paragraph 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within four weeks, directing respondent no.2 to decide it in accordance with law within a further six weeks after reasonable opportunity of hearing, and staying coercive action for eight weeks or until disposal of the objection, whichever is earlier.
facts: Nand Kishor filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court to quash recovery proceedings pursuant to a notice dated 19 August 2021 for realising Rs.53,632. None appeared for him even on the revised call. Standing counsel and counsel for respondent no.2, the distribution licensee, were present. Counsel for respondent no.2 stated on instruction that the petitioner could submit an objection before that respondent under paragraph 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, to be decided within a time-bound period.

holding_units.topic: objection to recovery notice — alternate remedy with stay
holding_units.holding: Where a consumer challenges a recovery notice by writ, and the licensee states that an objection under paragraph 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 may be filed and will be decided in a time-bound manner, the High Court may, without expressing any opinion on merits, dispose of the writ by granting liberty to file that objection within a stipulated period, directing disposal after reasonable opportunity of hearing, and staying coercive action for a limited period pending that disposal.

principle_tags.application: Writ disposed with liberty to file a paragraph 6.8 objection within four weeks; if filed, to be decided after hearing within six weeks; coercive action stayed for eight weeks or till disposal, whichever is earlier.
Court relegated the consumer to the paragraph 6.8 objection before respondent no.2 rather than examining the recovery notice on merits.
Demand of Rs.53,632 under the 19.08.2021 notice left to the statutory 6.8 objection route, to be decided in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: Validity of the notice dated 19.08.2021 and the demand of Rs.53,632
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits.
